draft.title: Strong and weak acids
card: Strong acid
An acid that ionises fully in water. Almost every molecule donates its proton, so HCl in water gives H⁺ (as H₃O⁺) and Cl⁻ ions, with almost no HCl left.
Weak acid
An acid that ionises only partly in water. Most molecules stay whole, and a small share donate a proton. Ethanoic acid is an example, and it forms an equilibrium.
Bases
The same split applies to bases. A strong base such as NaOH is fully dissociated into ions. A weak base such as NH₃ only partly reacts with water.
Strength is about how much ionises. Concentration is about how much acid is dissolved in a volume. A dilute solution of a strong acid and a concentrated solution of a weak acid are both possible.
draft.remember: Strength is the share that ionises. Concentration is the amount dissolved per volume.

a.q: Which statement best describes a weak acid in water?
opts: Only some of its molecules donate a proton to water
It is always a very dilute solution of acid
Its molecules all donate protons to water at once
It cannot donate any protons to water molecules
a.why: A weak acid ionises only partly, so most molecules stay whole while a few donate protons. Weak does not mean dilute, because strength describes ionisation and concentration describes how much is dissolved.
a.clue: Strength describes how much of the acid ionises.

b.q: Tariq has 0.01 M HCl and 2.0 M ethanoic acid. Which statement about these two solutions is correct?
opts: HCl is the stronger acid, but it is the more dilute one
Ethanoic acid is the stronger acid, as it is more concentrated
The two are equally strong because both are acids in water
HCl is the weaker acid because its solution is more dilute
b.why: HCl ionises fully, so it is a strong acid, even at 0.01 M. Ethanoic acid ionises only partly, so it is weak, even at 2.0 M. Tempting answers confuse concentration with strength.
b.clue: Ask how much ionises, not how much is dissolved.
